title: How Socialism Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain socialism: its core idea that the economy shapes society, how it differs from communism and capitalism, and the range of socialist types (utopian, market, Christian, communal). They trace its history from Thomas More's Utopia and Plato's Republic through Babeuf, the Industrial Revolution, communal experiments like Brook Farm and Robert Owen's New Lanark, New Harmony, the 1848 revolutions, the US socialist movement and Red Scare, Lenin and Stalin, Soviet central planning (Gosplan), postwar Britain and the NHS, Thatcher, and Canadian and US healthcare. They close with the idea of a mixed "third way" economy. The episode also includes a Squarespace ad, a podcast review shout-out, and a listener email about a near-accident in London.

segments.title: Opening banter and framing socialism
segments.summary: Hosts joke about socialism as a dirty word, note the laziness problem, attribute the 'it's the economy' idea to Marx and Engels, and introduce the economy-centered view of socialism versus capitalism.

segments.title: Thomas More's Utopia and early utopian ideas
segments.summary: Thomas More coined 'utopia' in 1516 with a fictional island of shared property, rotated houses, and six-hour workdays. Plato's Republic is described as an early blueprint with a governing class and planned economy. Utopian novels grew popular between 1700 and 1850.

segments.title: Babeuf, communism versus socialism, and definitions
segments.summary: Francois Noel Babeuf is considered an early socialist before being executed during the French Revolution. Communism is described as socialism's more militant or final stage, with socialism distributing by merit and communism by need. Market socialism in Yugoslavia and Hungary is mentioned.

segments.title: Pure definitions of socialism and private property
segments.summary: The hosts describe socialism in pure terms: no classes, central planning of production and distribution, and no private ownership of factories, with personal items like TVs still owned. Capitalism is contrasted through supply, demand, and competition.

segments.title: Industrial Revolution and early communal experiments
segments.summary: The Industrial Revolution widened wealth gaps and spurred socialist ideas. Brook Farm in Massachusetts (1840s) ended with a fire and bankruptcy by 1847. Shaker and Amish communities are mentioned, along with Christian socialist communes.

segments.title: Robert Owen: New Lanark and New Harmony
segments.summary: Wealthy capitalist Robert Owen tried socialist experiments at New Lanark in Scotland, then bought the Harmony, Indiana settlement and founded New Harmony, which lasted about two years. Owen is credited with child labor reforms and early preschool and public education.

segments.title: Luddites, 1848 revolutions, and socialism in the US
segments.summary: The Luddites are clarified as opponents of machines that took their jobs. The 1848 European revolutions are described as having lasting effects on Sweden, Denmark and others. Socialism in the US is traced to the Socialist Labor Party, founded in 1876 as the Workingmen's Party, and Eugene Debs's presidential vote.

segments.title: Lenin, Stalin, and Soviet central planning
segments.summary: Lenin implemented socialist policies after 1917 but backtracked toward a mixed economy. Stalin forced collectivization with heavy loss of life. Soviet Gosplan planning and the critique of central planning and information problems are described.

segments.title: Espionage Act, McCarthy era, and famous American socialists
segments.summary: The 1917 Espionage Act and the McCarthy era weakened US socialist groups. Figures said to identify as socialists include Albert Einstein, Saul Bellow, and Harry Belafonte.

segments.title: Britain post-war: Attlee, NHS, and Thatcher
segments.summary: Clement Attlee's Labour government nationalized industries and founded the National Health Service in 1948. Nationalized industries became unprofitable. Inflation and strikes in the 1970s led to Margaret Thatcher, who reduced spending and privatized industries.

segments.title: Squarespace sponsor read
segments.summary: Squarespace sponsor read offering website building and a free trial.

segments.title: Healthcare: Canada versus United States
segments.summary: Canadian single-payer healthcare is compared with the US market approach. Price discrepancies for MRIs are discussed, along with a story about quadruplets born in Montana.

segments.title: Socialism in modern life and the mixed economy
segments.summary: Government regulations and welfare programs are described as forms of socialism. Western nations are said to have a mixed or third-way economy, and the military is discussed as a socialist-like institution. Collectivist versus individualist framing is offered.

segments.title: Podcast review shout-out and listener email
segments.summary: The hosts thank Pod on Pod for a review, then read a listener email about being hit by a car in London while drunk.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close with contact information and a reminder to search howstuffworks.com.
